courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Augustine's Confessions
courses.description: This class will read and examine substantial portions of the Latin text of Augustine's autobiographical masterpiece, The Confessions, the most important of his writings, and a seminal work of Greco-Roman literature. Students will also read the entire text in English translation. Through background readings and lectures students will gain a broader understanding of the Late Antiquity, the end of the Roman Empire, the conflicts of Christianity and paganism, and the genres of biography and autobiography.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Independent Research in Latin
courses.description: This course allows a student to design and execute an independent research project under the supervision of a faculty member. Although the specifics will be determined on a case-by-case basis by the student and the faculty supervisor, the project will normally involve the careful study of key primary sources and engagement with relevant scholarship, and culminate in a major research paper (around 25 pages) or a suitable equivalent in another format (e.g., website, video). Permission of the Instructor.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Accelerated Elementary Latin
courses.description: An intensive introduction to Latin grammar and syntax, equivalent to LATN 101 and 102 . Students may not receive credit for the following course pairs: LATN 101 and 601 ; LATN 102 and 601 .

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Accelerated Intermediate Latin
courses.description: An intensive review of Latin grammar, along with vocabulary building and the development of reading and translation skills, equivalent to LATN 203 and 204 . Students may not receive credit for the following course pairs: LATN 203 and 602 ; LATN 204 and 602 .

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Introductory Latin Composition
courses.description: Review of Latin grammar and idiom, exercises in composition, introduction to stylistics.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Readings in Latin Literature of the Republic
courses.description: Selections from Roman comedy, Lucretius, Catullus, Cicero, Caesar, and/or Sallust, focusing on works on the M.A. and Ph.D. reading lists.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Readings in Latin Literature of the Augustan Age
courses.description: Selections from Vergil, Horace, the elegiac poets, Ovid, and/or Livy, focusing on works on the M.A. and Ph.D. reading lists.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Readings in Latin Literature of the Empire
courses.description: Selections from writers from the Neronian period through Apuleius, focusing on works on the M.A. and Ph.D. reading lists.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Readings in Latin Literature of Later Antiquity
courses.description: Selections from writers from the early 3rd to the early 5th century, including Tertullian, the Passio Perpetuae, Augustine's Confessions, the Scriptores Historiae Augustae, and Ammianus Marcellinus, focusing on works on the M.A. and Ph.D. reading lists.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Latin Textual Criticism
courses.description: Introduction to textual criticism of Latin texts. Addresses transmission, principles of editing, constructing and interpreting an apparatus criticus. Practical editorial experience working from original manuscripts, microfilms, and digital reproductions.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Readings in Medieval Latin Literature
courses.description: Survey of medieval Latin literature from its beginnings through the high Middle Ages.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Roman Historical Literature
courses.description: Study of Sallust, Caesar, Suetonius, or the minor historians of the empire.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Roman Dramatic Literature
courses.description: Study of the comedies of Plautus and Terence or the tragedies of Seneca.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Roman Lyric and Elegiac Poetry
courses.description: Study of the forms of lyric and elegiac poetry with special attention to Catullus, Horace, Tibullus, or Propertius.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Roman Satire
courses.description: Study of the development of satiric forms with special attention to Horace or Juvenal.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Ovid and Literary Theory
courses.description: Introduction to literary theory through a study of Ovid and scholarly approaches to his poetry.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Topics in Medieval Latin Literature
courses.description: Reading in selected medieval Latin prose and verse authors.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Vergil
courses.description: We will read the AENEID in Latin, with special attention to the War in Italy. We'll concern ourselves with a variety of topics: style and language; allusion, intertextuality, and the poem's relationship to various texts or traditions; the blending or clash or voices and genres, and possible ways of responding to perceived inconsistencies; and critical debates about the poem's attitude toward the strengths & weaknesses of the Roman people.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: The Roman Novel
courses.description: Selections from Petronius and/or Apuleius and related texts.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Special Reading
courses.description: With permission of the department, this course may be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: LATN

courses.description: Topics vary from year to year.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.
